A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same research work. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover all 23 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–C, without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments in Section 6, including image classification, self-supervised learning, posterior collapse and continual learning. Appendices B–C contain additional experiments and analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental outcomes in Section 6 and Appendices B–C, including performance measurements, reconstruction examples, resource measurements and NTK analyses.

M1.justification: The syre method is identical: static random parameter bias combined with weight decay, including the diagonal-weighted variant in Equations (6)–(7). No algorithmic component or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic regression and teacher-student settings, MNIST and permuted MNIST, Fashion MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Slippery-Ant tasks. No training or evaluation coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including W-fix, dropout and weight decay in Figure 4, W-asymmetric and sigma-asymmetric networks in Figure 12, and the PPO variants in Figure 6.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendices B–C retain identical preprocessing, model configurations, hyperparameters, sample sizes, rank thresholds and evaluation procedures. No protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The bias-scale and weight-decay sweeps, input/label-noise experiments, covariance-spectrum analyses, reconstruction examples, mode-connectivity experiments and NTK analyses are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is identical, including the standard deviation over 10 trials in Figure 3, averaging over five random seeds in Figure 6 and the plus/minus entries in Table 2.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted curves and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains last-layer accuracy of 22.2% for vanilla training and 31.7% for syre with sigma0 = 0.1.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Propositions 1–3, Theorems 1–5, corollary and Appendix A proofs are identical. No mathematical statement, derivation or proof is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about symmetry-induced capacity loss, symmetry removal without prior symmetry knowledge and applications across learning settings.

C2.justification: Interpretations and qualifications are unchanged, including the incomplete explanation of the self-supervised representation gap in Section 6.5 and the symmetry, optimization and overfitting tradeoff in Section 7.

D1.justification: Implementation guidance, hyperparameters, experimental details, A6000 GPU disclosure and the syre code-access information are unchanged. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and full set of cited works are identical. References that shift between pages 11–13 are relocated, not added or removed.

P1.justification: v4 adds a short Acknowledgements section recognizing NTT Research and IAIFI support through an NSF grant, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and the existing section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgement shifts the reference-list layout across pages 11–13, and the first-page margin stamp changes. All 14 figures and three tables retain identical content, formatting and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 adds funding attribution but retains identical methods, theory, experimental evidence, reproducibility details and scientific discussion, including the appendices. The acknowledgement and limited reference reflow do not materially change the paper's overall scientific quality or clarity.
